## 正文

## Dev Engineer Review

The source change replaces GEMM with elementwise rotary-frequency multiplication. This protects phase precision when TF32 is enabled. The change may alter performance, so benchmark the vision RoPE path if performance is a concern. No API changes are reported.

## QA Engineer Review

`tests/unittest/_torch/modeling/test_modeling_gemma4.py` adds a regression test for Gemma4 vision RoPE generation. The test rejects `aten.mm` and `aten.bmm` dispatch and compares cosine and sine outputs with a double-precision reference on a 64×64 grid. No integration test-list changes are shown. Coverage verdict: **sufficient**. Test execution results are unavailable.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/models/modeling_gemma4_vision.py`: Verify RoPE numerical accuracy and confirm that rotary-table generation does not dispatch GEMM operators. Check for unacceptable performance regression.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/modeling/test_modeling_gemma4.py`: Covers the TF32 precision regression and forbidden matrix-multiply dispatch. The unit test does not require an integration test-list entry.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

* Why?

TF32-enabled matrix multiplication can reduce rotary phase precision for the vision position embeddings.

* What?

Compute the rotary outer product elementwise and add a regression test that verifies no matrix-multiply operators are dispatched.
